note: Round numbering: PROGRESS.md rounds 1 to 5 are the old polish loop, 6 to 9 are the low spec loop, and this loop continues the overall count from 10. The polish loop's A/B/C rubric is superseded and kept in history only. The A items in rubric_A below are the SOUND rubric of this loop, not the old polish loop's A items.

attempted.1: A1, the product shell: title, how to fly, settings, pause, results, and a flight display replacing the developer HUD
attempted.2: A4 and A5, plus every defect the two round 1 reviewers raised
attempted.3: B5 focal hierarchy and B1 value bands, plus B4 for the grass and the two artefacts with a named mechanism
attempted.4: Both round 3 reviewers' lists: the shadow map rendered twice, ridge value collapse, gate glow ladder, cloud clipping, unlit flowers, the meadow's straight edge, two ink mechanisms, camera near and prepass depth precision
attempted.5: The round 4 review's list: the composer had no antialiasing at all, ring 0 sat inside the tree canopy band, clouds still clipped at 1.000 and held 63 percent of the frame's bright area, and the title scrim crushed the lower two thirds
attempted.6: Low spec loop round 1: build the instrument and publish the cost ledger for P1 to P10 across three views at two resolutions. No renderer behaviour changed.
attempted.7: Low spec loop round 2: P5, the furthest over budget at 2.43x. Packed the prepass to one RGBA8 target, moved antialiasing into the edge pass, folded the OutputPass into the grade, dropped depth buffers from bloom targets.
attempted.8: Both round 7 reviewers' lists: the default framebuffer missing from the P5 ledger, mebibytes printed as megabytes, the 1080p derivation scaling a resolution independent shadow map, antialiasing that blurred across the edge instead of filtering along it, and five stale numbers in comments.
attempted.9: The value ladder: G1, G2, G3 and G5 on the ridges together. FOG_FAR 780 to 2200, four ridge rings re-anchored with a hue only light model at equal luminance, gate glow ladder raised.
attempted.10: The two missing instruments. scripts/audio-probe.js renders the real audio graph on an OfflineAudioContext and measures it; scripts/shots.js writes an aim sidecar beside every PNG recording which gate the race actually wants. No feature. Both instruments calibrated against predictable signals before any claim was made from them.

open_from_reviewers_not_yet_fixed: B2: mountain silhouettes carry no ink at all. post.js OutlineShader fades edges from d0 0.16 to 0.42, about 320 m to 840 m, and cone on cone depth deltas never reach the threshold
B2: the grass ink suppression eats the gate plinth's contact line with the meadow into dashes, exactly where a pilot judges ground clearance
B2: a flag cloth passes through a tree canopy while its own pole passes in front of the same canopy
B2: canopy edges carry a 2 to 3 px pale rim inside the dark ink line, a dark light dark fringe that reads as a compositing error
B4 and B6: mountain rings 2 and 3 never appear in any rendered frame because rings 0 and 1 occlude them, so half the aerial perspective palette is dead code
B4: the mountains are unlit flat colour. Values are reliable, but the largest mass in the frame has no warm light and no cool shadow
B4: water has no light model and every band is cool including the lit crests; its bands key off radius from the lake centre rather than depth, so from altitude it reads as a bullseye
B4: the gate frame navy 0x2a3352 shows a 3 percent luminance difference between its sunlit top face and its vertical face, so the structure is a flat cutout
B4: the rim term in celmat.js is step(0.5, rim) with no sun term, so it floods whole grazing angle faces and is brightest on the shadow side
B5: gate 2 can be occluded by a tree canopy, and nothing in the frame reads as the track tier between the next gate and the landmarks
B5: the amber accent means gate ring, OSD gate counter, banner, settings heading and throttle bar all at once
B6 root cause: makeHeightField forces height to zero within 30 m of every point on the circuit, so the flight area is a plane and there is nothing between a 250 mm quad and a 200 m mountain
B6: the lake has no shoreline. A dead straight far edge butts into the mountain silhouette, grass stands inside the water, a rock floats half submerged
B1 and B6: the 70 m cream sand shore, one flat value with no detail
B3: never reviewed. No frame has been captured at racing speed, and the reviewer could not fly through gate 1 to judge mid course hierarchy
performance: 204 static gate meshes and 72 flag cloths are 77 percent of the draw calls, and the merger is already in scene.js
performance: the grass fragment shader spends 16 shadow map compares and 12 noise hashes per fragment on two values that cannot vary across a 3 cm blade
performance: grass.frustumCulled false submits 552000 triangles and 32 MB of vertex buffer every frame regardless of view
performance: load is a 2195 ms synchronous stall, dominated by 67 million distance to track evaluations
performance: the attract view is 701 draw calls against 237 in flight, and round 4's 9 percent increase there is still unaccounted for
OSD: the pack falls 25.2 V to 18.1 V in about 3.2 s of full throttle, which makes the pack gauge close to useless as a readout
C1 to C5 untouched: no latency measurement, no ground effect, no impact feedback, no particles anywhere in the render, audio is still a sawtooth per motor
